summary: Checked on 2026-09-13 against primary sources where possible. (1) TCBB has been renamed. Since 2025 it publishes as 'IEEE Transactions on Computational Biology and Bioinformatics' (IEEE only, no ACM in the title), with a new electronic ISSN 2998-4165 and DOI prefix 10.1109/tcbbio. It is a hybrid journal: the 2026 IEEE APC list gives a $2,800 open-access fee and $220 per page beyond 12 pages for a regular paper. (2) IEEE CIBCB 2026 already took place (31 Aug - 2 Sep 2026, Athens, Greece, in person only). Its full-paper deadline was 30 Apr 2026. Accepted and presented papers go to IEEE Xplore; papers whose authors do not present are archived but not indexed. CIBCB 2025 (Tainan, Taiwan) is in Crossref/IEEE Xplore. No official CIBCB 2027 page was found. (3) JBHI is hybrid ($2,800 OA fee). TNSRE has been fully gold open access since 2020, with a $2,160 APC for 2026 submissions. IEEE Access charges $2,160 (5% off for IEEE members, 20% for society members). (4) IEEE policy requires disclosing AI-generated content (text, figures, images, code) in the acknowledgments, naming the AI system and the sections it affected. Editing and grammar help is outside the policy, but disclosure is still recommended. Reviewers may not put manuscripts into public AI platforms. IEEE requires original work, bans concurrent submission to multiple publications, and sets three human-style authorship criteria. None of the IEEE pages retrieved say in so many words that an AI cannot be an author; that point is supported only by the authorship criteria and by secondary sources. (5) IEEE lets authors post preprints on arXiv, TechRxiv, or not-for-profit servers approved by the IEEE PSPB, and does not count this as prior publication. The IEEE documents retrieved do not name bioRxiv. (6) OSF registrations are frozen and time-stamped, can be embargoed for up to 4 years, and get a DOI when public; a Simulation Studies template exists. Zenodo archives a GitHub release when the release is published, gives each version its own identifier, and ignores CITATION.cff if a .zenodo.json file is present. The current CFF spec release is 1.2.0 (2021-08-09). (7) Non-IEEE alternatives were checked: PLOS Computational Biology (Methods and Software article types, $3,165), JOSS (free; requires 6 months of public development history), eLife (Reviewed Preprint model, $3,750, waivable), Frontiers in Neuroinformatics (APC CHF 3,150 for A-type articles), Neuroinformatics (Springer; model and fees not confirmed from the publisher). ReScience C publishes only replications, so it does not fit the main NeuroSem paper. Tool note: most page contents were read through WebFetch, whose model summarises the page. Crossref, OpenAlex, the GitHub API and the IEEE PDFs were parsed directly.

venues.scope_summary: Multidisciplinary, online-only, gold fully open-access IEEE journal. The scope was taken from IEEE search snippets and the APC page context, not a dedicated scope page.

AI-generated content must be disclosed in the acknowledgments, naming the AI system and sections (grammar editing generally exempt). Expanded versions of the authors' own conference papers are allowed if similarity is below 35% and the relationship is disclosed.

ieee_ai_policy.summary: IEEE policy (journals, conferences, magazines and books author centers, plus IEEE Open): any AI-generated content in an article (text, figures, images and code, among others) must be disclosed in the acknowledgments section. The disclosure names the AI system and identifies the specific sections that use AI-generated content, with a brief explanation of how much the system was used. Using AI for editing and grammar enhancement is generally outside the policy's intent, but disclosure is still recommended. The IEEE Books page also warns authors to double-check AI output and not to run grammar tools over reference lists. The peer-review side forbids processing a manuscript under review, or information about it, through a public AI platform. The IEEE Open version of the guideline is dated 16 April 2024. NeuroSem implications: the handoff's wording 'substantive generative-AI use' is narrower than IEEE's text, which covers any AI-generated content, including code shown in the article. Claude Code's role in building the software, any AI-drafted text or figures, and the agent case study should all be disclosed in the acknowledgments, even if pure copy-editing would be exempt. IEEE also leaves the author accountable for disclosure.

ieee_authorship_and_originality.summary: Authorship (IEEE Author Center, Ethical Requirements): an author must meet all three criteria. They (1) made a significant intellectual contribution to theory, system or experimental design, prototype development, and/or data analysis and interpretation; (2) drafted or revised the article for intellectual content; and (3) approved the final version as accepted. Contributors who fall short go in the acknowledgments. The corresponding author makes sure the author list is right, gets every co-author's assent and approval of the final version, and keeps co-authors informed. None of the IEEE primary pages retrieved (journal submission policies, ethical requirements, conference submission policies, magazines and books policies, IEEE Open AI guideline) explicitly says an AI system cannot be an author. That statement appears only in secondary sources (a CASRAI summary and search-engine syntheses). The handoff's 'only humans can be authors' therefore rests, on the IEEE primary evidence gathered, on the authorship criteria rather than an explicit AI clause; the explicit clause is unverified. Originality and duplicate submission: authors should submit only original work that has not appeared elsewhere and is not under review at another refereed publication, and must disclose all prior publications and current submissions. IEEE defines multiple submission as the same article being under active consideration at two or more publications at once; individual IEEE units decide whether to allow it, with disclosure. IEEE accepts that work evolves from workshop to conference to journal, provided the new submission cites the earlier work and explains how it differs. IEEE Access sets a similarity threshold below 35% for expanded conference papers. Plagiarism is a serious breach of professional conduct. The handoff's statement that IEEE requires original work and bans simultaneous submission of substantially similar manuscripts matches this policy. The PSPB Operations Manual section 8.2.1 page (ieee.org/publications/rights/section-821) returned an empty body and was not read directly.

preprint_policy.summary: IEEE Post-Publication Policies and the IEEE Article Sharing and Posting Policies PDF. Before submission, authors may post preprints on their personal or employer website, arXiv.org, TechRxiv.org, or any not-for-profit preprint server approved by the IEEE Publication Services and Products Board (PSPB). IEEE does not treat such posting as prior publication. Preprints on other locations should be removed after IEEE publishes, where possible. On acceptance, earlier posted versions must be replaced by the full citation with DOI or by the accepted version with DOI, and posted accepted articles must carry the IEEE copyright notice. Accepted versions may be posted on personal or employer sites, arXiv, TechRxiv or funder repositories; the funder-repository embargo is 24 months unless the funder requires less. For non-OA final published articles, authors may not post the version of record. Gold OA articles under CC BY or CC BY-NC-ND may be posted anywhere under that licence. bioRxiv is not named in any IEEE document retrieved; whether it is a PSPB-approved server is unverified. bioRxiv's own FAQ says most basic-research journals accept preprinted manuscripts, that computational work is welcome as full research papers but bare software announcements are not, and that it offers several licences (from all rights reserved to CC0). For an IEEE target, arXiv is the explicitly permitted choice. If bioRxiv is wanted, confirm with the chosen journal's editor first.

preregistration_and_archiving.name: OSF Registries / OSF Preregistration
preregistration_and_archiving.notes: OSF help pages: a registration is a frozen, time-stamped version of a project that cannot be edited or deleted. Withdrawal keeps basic metadata (title, contributors, DOI) plus the justification but removes the content. Embargoes can last up to four years. Public registrations get a DOI automatically, which serves as the registration number. Admins have 48 hours to approve before automatic approval. Templates include OSF Preregistration, Open-Ended Registration, Secondary Data, Simulation Studies and Registered Report Protocol; the Simulation Studies and Secondary Data templates look most relevant for NeuroSem's M8 preregistration. The help pages do not state a cost. Overview page: https://help.osf.io/article/330-welcome-to-registrations. The osf.io/registries landing page itself was not fetched because it is JavaScript-rendered.

preregistration_and_archiving.name: Zenodo GitHub integration
preregistration_and_archiving.notes: Zenodo docs: with a connected GitHub account, go to profile menu > GitHub > Sync now and toggle the repository on (enable-repository page). Publishing a GitHub release triggers archiving (github-upload page), and software records are also archived in Software Heritage. Failed releases show errors in Zenodo, often from bad CITATION.cff metadata; the docs recommend validating with cffconvert (PyPI 2.0.0 at retrieval). Metadata: if a .zenodo.json file exists, Zenodo uses only it and ignores CITATION.cff entirely. Zenodo implements a subset of CFF fields: cff-version, title, version, license, type, abstract, message, authors (given-names, family-names, affiliation, orcid), keywords. Versioning (help.zenodo.org/docs/deposit/manage-versions/): each new version is a new record with its own persistent identifier, linked to all other versions. Whether a separate 'concept DOI' covers all versions and resolves to the latest could not be read from Zenodo directly (zenodo.org/help/versioning returned 504, the Zenodo API returned 403); it rests only on a search snippet and is unverified here. Whether private repositories are supported is not stated in the pages retrieved (unverified).

preregistration_and_archiving.name: Citation File Format (CITATION.cff)
preregistration_and_archiving.notes: GitHub REST API: the spec repository citation-file-format/citation-file-format is licensed CC-BY-4.0, its latest release is 1.2.0 (published 2021-08-09T17:11:07Z), last pushed 2026-01-20, not archived. The schema.json on main has $id https://citation-file-format.github.io/1.2.0/schema.json (JSON Schema draft-07) and requires authors, cff-version, message and title. The README example uses cff-version 1.2.0 with identifiers for an all-versions DOI and a version-specific DOI. GitHub Docs: a CITATION.cff at the root of the default branch adds a 'Cite this repository' link with APA and BibTeX output, and the optional preferred-citation field can point readers to a paper instead of the software. Project concept DOI badge in README: 10.5281/zenodo.1003149 (not resolved separately).

alternative_non_ieee_venues.name: PLOS Computational Biology (ALTERNATIVE, non-IEEE)
alternative_non_ieee_venues.notes: Scope: computational methods (including AI/ML) for understanding biological systems at all scales. Relevant article types: Methods articles (new methods with broad potential for biological insight) and Software articles (significant open-source tools giving new biological insight). Both require code, data and details enough to reproduce. Fully OA (OpenAlex: in DOAJ). Publication fee is $3,165 for research articles, charged at the rate in force on the submission date (plos.org/publication-fees). Fee assistance and Research4Life options exist. Probably the most natural fit if NeuroSem yields methodological insight into neuron-model behaviour.

alternative_non_ieee_venues.name: Neuroinformatics (Springer) (ALTERNATIVE, non-IEEE)
alternative_non_ieee_venues.notes: Crossref: title 'Neuroinformatics', publisher Springer-Verlag, ISSNs 1539-2791 / 1559-0089. OpenAlex: not fully OA, not in DOAJ, homepage springer.com journal 12021, with an APC figure of 4,890 USD that probably refers to a hybrid OA option (unverified). The publisher page (link.springer.com/journal/12021) redirected to a Springer login/cookie wall and could not be read, so scope, article types and fees are unverified from the publisher. The title is a strong topical match for NeuroML model-testing infrastructure.

alternative_non_ieee_venues.name: Frontiers in Neuroinformatics (ALTERNATIVE, non-IEEE)
alternative_non_ieee_venues.notes: Publisher Frontiers Media SA; fully OA and in DOAJ (OpenAlex). Scope (journal page, model-summarised): neuroinformatics methods, brain data analysis and computational modelling of neural systems. APCs listed in CHF: A-type 3,150, B-type 2,500, C-type free. Which article types fall into A, B or C was not verified. Institutional partnerships and discounts for low and lower-middle income countries are available. The journal's article-type list (e.g. whether a 'Technology and Code' type exists) was not verified.

alternative_non_ieee_venues.name: eLife (ALTERNATIVE, non-IEEE)
alternative_non_ieee_venues.notes: Current model: submissions selected for review are published as a Reviewed Preprint with an eLife Assessment, the public reviews and the author response. Authors can later choose to make it a Version of Record. eLife works with authors to make reviewed submissions available as preprints. Publication fee is $3,750, waived for anyone who cannot afford it. The fit depends on neuroscience significance, not software engineering alone.

alternative_non_ieee_venues.name: Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS) (ALTERNATIVE, non-IEEE; software paper companion)
alternative_non_ieee_venues.notes: Diamond OA with no fees. Requirements: research software under an OSI-approved licence, feature-complete and maintainable, with evidence of research impact or external use, and at least six months of public development history before submission. Minor utilities and thin API wrappers are not eligible. A Crossref DOI is minted on acceptance and papers are archived in Portico. AI policy: authors must include an AI usage disclosure (tools, scope of help, confirmation of human review); reviewers may use AI only for non-substantive tasks, with disclosure. This suits a software paper for the NeuroSem package after the M10 release, not the scientific results. The six-month history rule affects timing.

alternative_non_ieee_venues.name: ReScience C (ALTERNATIVE, non-IEEE; limited fit)
alternative_non_ieee_venues.notes: Publishes only explicit replications of previously published computational research with new open-source implementations. Platinum OA (no fees), with open review in GitHub issues. It does not accept original methods or software papers, so it is not a venue for the main NeuroSem paper. It could suit a separate replication of a published neuron model if one arises.

handoff_assumption_issues: OUTDATED: the handoff names the target 'IEEE/ACM Transactions on Computational Biology and Bioinformatics (TCBB)'. Crossref shows it has published since 2025 (vol. 22) as 'IEEE Transactions on Computational Biology and Bioinformatics', with new e-ISSN 2998-4165 and DOI prefix 10.1109/tcbbio. Update the name in PLAN.md and in any future cover letter. ACM's removal as co-publisher comes from a secondary source only.
UNCERTAIN: TCBB's scope was not confirmed from an IEEE primary page (JavaScript-only or blocked). Re-check scope and recent papers before calling it the 'best IEEE journal fit'.

INCOMPLETE: the handoff mentions open-access fees only for IEEE Access. TCBB and JBHI are hybrid ($2,800 optional OA fee in 2026, plus overlength charges of $220/page for TCBB beyond 12 pages). TNSRE is fully gold OA with a mandatory $2,160 APC. Under the zero-budget constraint, subscription (non-OA) publication in a hybrid journal avoids the APC, but page overlength charges may still apply.

TIMING: the handoff refers to 'a future IEEE CIBCB'. The 2026 edition ran 31 Aug - 2 Sep 2026 in Athens (deadline 30 Apr 2026), so the earliest option is a 2027 edition, whose dates, location and call are unverified.

COST/LOGISTICS: CIBCB requires in-person presentation (no-show papers are left out of IEEE Xplore) and a full non-student registration (EUR 700-930 in 2026), plus travel. This conflicts with a zero-budget constraint unless funding is found.

OK WITH NUANCE: the handoff says 'substantive generative-AI use must be disclosed'. IEEE's text is broader: any AI-generated content in the article, including text, figures, images and code, must be disclosed in the acknowledgments with the system named and the sections identified; only editing and grammar help is generally exempt, and even that is recommended for disclosure. NeuroSem should plan a detailed AI acknowledgment covering Claude Code's development role and the agent case study.

UNCERTAIN: 'Only humans can be authors' is not stated in those words on any IEEE primary page retrieved. It follows from IEEE's three authorship criteria and matches secondary summaries of IEEE policy. Keep the practice, but cite the authorship criteria rather than claiming an explicit IEEE clause.

CONFIRMED: IEEE requires original work, bans concurrent consideration by two or more publications, and requires disclosure of prior and related publications. A conference paper (e.g. CIBCB) can later be extended into a journal paper if it is cited and the differences are explained; IEEE Access requires similarity below 35%.

GAP: the handoff does not address preprints. IEEE explicitly allows arXiv and TechRxiv, and not-for-profit servers approved by IEEE PSPB. bioRxiv is not named, so for an IEEE target prefer arXiv or confirm with the editor. After acceptance, preprints must carry the IEEE copyright notice and DOI.

GAP/ACTION: M10's 'DOI archive' works with the Zenodo GitHub integration: a published release is archived automatically and each version gets its own identifier. If a .zenodo.json exists, Zenodo ignores CITATION.cff, so keep a single source of metadata or keep both files in sync. Zenodo supports only a subset of CFF fields.
OK: CITATION.cff in the repository tree should use cff-version 1.2.0, still the latest spec release (2021-08-09). Validate with cffconvert (2.0.0 on PyPI).

OK WITH ACTION: M8 preregistration is feasible on OSF Registries: frozen, time-stamped, embargo up to 4 years, DOI when public. Consider the 'Simulation Studies' template. Registrations cannot be edited, only withdrawn with metadata kept, so the held-out split hashes and analysis plan must be final before submission.
TIMING: if a JOSS software paper is considered, JOSS requires at least six months of public development history and evidence of research impact.
